enzyme_name: Aryl (phenol) sulfotransferase SULT1A2 / N-acetylserotonin sulfotransferase
organism_context: Human cytosolic SULT1A subfamily; MetaCyc assigns RXN-11059 to Homo sapiens sulfotransferase 1A2.
rationale: Cytosolic SULT1A enzymes are single-domain PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transferases with one catalytic activity; no second catalytic function is reported for SULT1A1/1A2.
direction_note: MetaCyc writes the reaction irreversibly as N-acetylserotonin + PAPS -> N-acetylserotonin sulfate + PAP + H+, and PAPS-driven sulfuryl transfer with PAP release is physiologically one-way, matching the council's '>'.

enzyme_name: Methionine gamma-lyase / PLP-dependent C-Se lyase (EC 4.4.1.11 type)
organism_context: MetaCyc records no enzyme for RXN-11063 and cross-references EC 4.4.1.11 (bacterial MegL/MdeA, Arabidopsis AT1G64660); seleno-amino acid detoxification/volatilization III.
rationale: Enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry and MetaCyc's EC cross-reference, not confirmed; methionine gamma-lyase runs alpha,gamma- and alpha,beta-eliminations on several substrates but that is one broad-specificity catalytic activity, not two.
direction_note: The real MetaCyc reaction is Se-methyl-L-selenocysteine + H2O -> methaneselenol + pyruvate + ammonium; ModelSEED kept only the seleno-amino acid and a mis-mapped dimethyl diselenide, discarding the pyruvate/ammonium release that makes the lyase step irreversible in the council's '>' direction.

enzyme_name: Methionine gamma-lyase / PLP-dependent C-Se lyase (EC 4.4.1.11 type)
organism_context: MetaCyc records no enzyme for RXN-11064 and cross-references EC 4.4.1.11; seleno-amino acid detoxification/volatilization I (plants, AraCyc).
rationale: As for rxn21363, the catalyst is inferred from chemistry plus MetaCyc's EC cross-reference; methionine gamma-lyase is a single-activity PLP elimination enzyme.
direction_note: MetaCyc's equation is Se-methyl-Se-L-methionine + H2O -> dimethyl selenide + 2-oxobutanoate + ammonium + H+; ModelSEED dropped water, 2-oxobutanoate and ammonium, hiding the irreversible gamma-elimination that volatilizes selenium in the council's '>' direction.

enzyme_name: Arabinogalactan UDP-galactofuranosyltransferase 2 (GlfT2, Rv3808c)
organism_context: Mycobacterium tuberculosis / M. smegmatis galactan polymerase; MetaCyc assigns RXN-11077 (EC 2.4.1.288) to GlfT2.
rationale: GlfT2 is one polypeptide that alternately installs beta-(1->5) and beta-(1->6) Galf linkages - two separately numbered catalytic activities - and the literature consistently calls it a bifunctional galactofuranosyltransferase; the two activities share a single active site but are distinct transfers, not a moonlighting role.
direction_note: Both activities run the same way (UDP-Galf consumed, UDP released), so bifunctionality creates no reverse flux; MetaCyc writes the polymerization irreversibly toward galactan, i.e. the council's '>'.

enzyme_name: Arabinofuranan 3-O-alpha-D-arabinofuranosyltransferase AftC (EC 2.4.2.47)
organism_context: Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv (MetaCyc assigns RXN-11092 to AftC); originally characterised from M. smegmatis.
rationale: AftC is a single-activity alpha(1->3) branching arabinofuranosyltransferase using decaprenylphospho-beta-D-arabinofuranose; the arabinan AraTs (AftA/AftB/AftC/AftD, EmbA/B) are each one-activity enzymes acting sequentially, with no reported fused second activity.
direction_note: Polyprenyl-phospho-sugar glycosyl transfer with decaprenyl phosphate release is irreversible; MetaCyc writes DPA + linear arabinan -> branched arabinan + DP, which is the ModelSEED left-to-right sense and the council's '>'.

enzyme_name: Terminal beta(1->2) arabinofuranosyltransferase AftB (Rv3805c)
organism_context: Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv; MetaCyc assigns RXN-11093 to AftB (inferred by functional complementation, Seidel et al.).
rationale: AftB is the single-activity capping arabinofuranosyltransferase that adds terminal beta(1->2) Araf residues; no second catalytic activity is reported on the same chain.
direction_note: As for AftC, decaprenylphospho-arabinose donation with DP release is one-way; MetaCyc's arrow consumes DPA, matching the council's '>' rather than ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: unknown (MetaCyc 'alpha-D-galacturonate 1-phosphate synthase'; no enzyme or gene recorded)
organism_context: L-ascorbate biosynthesis V (Euglena, D-galacturonate pathway), MetaCyc RXN-11147.
rationale: MetaCyc states 'No enzyme has been identified for this reaction in this database' and assigns no EC, so there is no protein to classify; the step is a pathway inference rather than a characterised activity.
direction_note: The entry's own name makes alpha-D-galacturonate 1-phosphate the product and MetaCyc writes UDP-GalA -> GalA-1-P, i.e. the council's '>'; the equation drops the UMP that should balance it, which is why the thermodynamic estimators see a large positive dG.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous intramolecular lactonization
organism_context: 4-hydroxycoumarin formation from cis-enol-3-oxomelilotoyl-CoA; MetaCyc RXN-11173.
rationale: MetaCyc's entry reads verbatim 'This reaction can occur spontaneously. No enzyme is required or has been identified', so there is no catalysing protein to classify.
direction_note: MetaCyc writes cis-enol-3-oxomelilotoyl-CoA -> 4-hydroxycoumarin + CoA irreversibly; thioester-releasing cyclization only runs that way, the council's '>'.

enzyme_name: Sterol 24-C-methyltransferase (SMT; SMT2 / SMT1 / Erg6p)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana SMT2 (AraCyc cross-reference); the same probe chemistry is reported for yeast Erg6p and Trypanosoma brucei SMT.
rationale: 26,27-Dehydrozymosterol is a mechanism-probe substrate of sterol C24-methyltransferase; Zhou & Nes show SMT2 converts it into two C28 products including a 3beta,24beta-diol (C28H46O2 - exactly ModelSEED's '24-alkyl sterol 2/3'). Nes explicitly reports a single active centre catalysing consecutive C1-transfers, so iterated methylation is not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: AdoMet/AdoHcy are collapsed into a formal 'methanol' (CH3 from SAM plus OH from water), removing the SAM -> SAH step that makes C24 methylation irreversible toward the 24-alkyl sterol, i.e. the council's '>'.

enzyme_name: Sterol 24-C-methyltransferase (SMT; SMT2 / SMT1 / Erg6p)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana SMT2 (AraCyc cross-reference); companion entry to RXN-11202 for the second 26,27-DHZ product.
rationale: Same enzyme and same mechanism-probe substrate as rxn21491 - SMT2 gives two C28 products from 26,27-dehydrozymosterol, which MetaCyc enters as '24-alkyl sterol 2' and '24-alkyl sterol 3'. Multiple products from one active site is not bifunctionality.
direction_note: As for rxn21491, SAM/SAH are abstracted into 'methanol', hiding the irreversibility of the methyl transfer that runs toward the 24-alkyl sterol (the council's '>').

enzyme_name: 3-Ketoacyl-CoA synthase (FAE1/KCS-type fatty acid elongase condensing enzyme)
organism_context: Plant seed microsomal elongase (Brassicaceae FAE1/KCS family); inferred from the C18:1 -> C20:1 chemistry, MetaCyc RXN-11229.
rationale: Enzyme identity is inferred from the chemistry (two-carbon elongation of oleate to cis-11-eicosenoate), not confirmed: the MetaCyc entry is not in the ModelSEED provenance dump and names no enzyme. The KCS condensing enzyme carries a single activity; the other three elongase steps (KCR, HCD, ECR) sit on separate polypeptides, so the elongase is a complex, not a fused multifunctional chain.
direction_note: Malonyl-CoA condensation with CO2 release makes elongation one-way, oleate -> icosenoate (the council's '>'); the equation as written has no C2 donor, NADPH or CO2 at all, so no thermodynamic estimate of it is meaningful.

enzyme_name: 3-Ketoacyl-CoA synthase (hydroxy-fatty-acid elongase condensing enzyme, PfKCS18/FAE1-type)
organism_context: Physaria (Lesquerella) fendleri seed; densipolic (18:2-OH) -> auricolic (20:2-OH) is the diene counterpart of the ricinoleic -> lesquerolic elongation. MetaCyc records no enzyme for RXN-11235.
rationale: Catalyst inferred from chemistry only - MetaCyc lists no enzyme and even its compound records are suspect (auricolate carries a C22H39O3 formula). The KCS condensing enzyme is single-activity and works within a four-protein elongase complex.
direction_note: MetaCyc writes this one as reversible ('densipolate = auricolate'), but the underlying reaction is an irreversible malonyl-CoA elongation that can only run densipolate -> auricolate, the council's '>'.

enzyme_name: unknown (MetaCyc RXN-11274 has no enzyme and no EC)
organism_context: Monoterpenoid/fenchol biosynthesis I (PWY-6437); substrate is MetaCyc CPD-685 (-)-endo-fenchol, product CPD-12223 beta-fenchene.
rationale: No enzyme, gene or EC is recorded for this step, so there is nothing to classify; the related characterised activity in the pathway is a monoterpene synthase acting on geranyl diphosphate, not on fenchol.
direction_note: MetaCyc's arrow runs fenchol -> beta-fenchene (the council's '>'), and dehydration rather than hydration of a bridged bicyclic alcohol is the accessible direction; the water of dehydration is missing from the equation (and MetaCyc's beta-fenchene record carries a C12H20 formula against fenchol's C10H18O).

enzyme_name: unknown (estolide-forming acyltransferase/lipase; MetaCyc records no enzyme for RXN-11304)
organism_context: Lesquerella (Physaria) seed oil estolide formation.
rationale: MetaCyc states 'No enzyme has been identified for this reaction in this database' for lesquerella oil + 2 dodecanoate -> triglyceride estolide + 2 H2O; no protein to classify.
direction_note: MetaCyc writes the condensation toward the estolide (the council's '>'), but written from free laurate rather than an activated acyl donor the ester bond formation looks near-equilibrium, which is exactly why eQuilibrator calls it '<'.

enzyme_name: unknown
organism_context: Estolide formation from oleate; MetaCyc RXN-11308 is absent from the ModelSEED MetaCyc provenance dump and the live entry is no longer reachable.
rationale: No enzyme is recorded anywhere for this entry and the chemistry is not coherent, so no catalyst can be identified or classified.
direction_note: Three oleates cannot condense into an estolide with release of CO2, and esterification releases rather than consumes water; with no enzyme and a non-balancing equation neither direction can be defended on enzymology.

enzyme_name: Cytochrome P450 fatty-acid omega-hydroxylase (CYP94A family; MetaCyc provisional EC 1.14.14.M34)
organism_context: Plant medium-chain fatty acid omega-hydroxylases, e.g. Vicia sativa CYP94A1 (laurate) and CYP94A2 (C10-C14); MetaCyc groups RXN-11325 with the generic fatty-acid omega-hydroxylase EC 1.14.14.M34.
rationale: MetaCyc's real equation is decanoate + O2 + reduced NADPH-hemoprotein reductase -> 10-hydroxydecanoate + oxidised reductase + H2O - a classic microsomal P450 monooxygenase. The P450 carries one catalytic activity and takes electrons from a physically separate NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase, so it is not a fused bifunctional chain; the exact CYP isoform is inferred rather than confirmed.
direction_note: O2 and the hemoprotein reductase have been deleted and free NADP+/NADPH substituted on the wrong sides, which is the only reason the entry reads as a reversible dehydrogenation; P450 omega-hydroxylation runs only decanoate -> 10-hydroxydecanoate, the council's '>'. ModelSEED also carries the intact version of this reaction separately (rxn41541).

enzyme_name: Peptidoglycan (lipid II) glutamate amidotransferase MurT-GatD complex
organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Mycobacterium tuberculosis (D-iGlu amidation of lipid II).
rationale: Amidation is run by a bi-enzymatic complex of two separate polypeptides - GatD is the glutaminase, MurT the ATP-dependent Mur-ligase-family amidotransferase - so by the multi-subunit exclusion this is a complex, not a bifunctional enzyme; MurT, which performs this step, carries the single ligase activity.
direction_note: ATP/ADP+Pi and the glutamine nitrogen donor are absent (MetaCyc even splits the step into an ATP-dependent gamma-glutamyl phosphorylation followed by amidation), so an irreversible ATP-driven amidation reads here as a reversible hydration; the enzyme only makes D-iGln, the council's '>'.

enzyme_name: Glutamine-dependent asparagine synthase AsnH/AsnB (peptidoglycan D-Asp amidotransferase)
distinct_activities: N-terminal class-II (Ntn) glutaminase: L-glutamine + H2O -> L-glutamate + NH3 (EC 3.5.1.2-type)
C-terminal ATP-dependent amido-ligase (asparagine synthase, EC 6.3.5.4-type) that amidates the beta-D-Asp side chain
organism_context: Lactococcus lactis AsnH identified by Veiga et al.; the same amidation decorates the D-Asp cross-bridge of Enterococcus faecium peptidoglycan (MetaCyc PWY-6470).
rationale: Veiga et al. show asnH, an asparagine synthetase B homologue, amidates peptidoglycan D-Asp; AsnB-family synthases are single chains with two spatially separate active sites (glutaminase and ATP-dependent synthetase) linked by an intramolecular ammonia tunnel - two genuine catalytic activities on one polypeptide.
direction_note: Both domains push the same way - glutamine hydrolysis plus ATP cleavage drive amidation - so amide hydrolysis back to D-Asp is not this enzyme's reaction; the equation omits glutamine and ATP, which is the only reason it looks reversible.

enzyme_name: Peptidoglycan (lipid II) glutamate amidotransferase MurT-GatD complex
organism_context: Gram-positive lipid II tetrapeptide D-iGlu amidation (S. aureus, S. pneumoniae, E. faecium; MetaCyc PWY-6470).
rationale: Same catalyst as rxn21650 acting on the tetrapeptide lipid II: a two-polypeptide MurT/GatD complex, excluded from 'bifunctional' by the multi-subunit rule; MurT alone carries the activity for this step.
direction_note: The ATP that drives amidation is missing from the equation, so the irreversible D-Glu -> D-iGln conversion (the council's '>') is rendered as a near-equilibrium hydration.

enzyme_name: 15-cis-Phytoene desaturase (PDS, plant-type; EC 1.3.5.5)
organism_context: Plants, algae and cyanobacteria (plastoquinone-dependent plant-type desaturase); MetaCyc assigns RXN-11355 to EC 1.3.5.5.
rationale: PDS introduces two successive double bonds (phytoene -> phytofluene -> 9,15,9'-tri-cis-zeta-carotene) using one FAD-dependent active site; that is iterated catalysis of the same activity, not a second catalytic function. Called from established enzymology plus the EC assignment.
direction_note: Desaturation is coupled to plastoquinone reduction that is continuously reoxidised by PTOX/the photosynthetic chain, pulling the reaction toward zeta-carotene - the council's '>' - regardless of the near-zero standard dG.

enzyme_name: Gibberellin A9 carboxyl methyltransferase GAMT1/GAMT2 (SABATH family, EC 2.1.1.275)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana (AraCyc cross-reference) and GAMT orthologues across seed plants.
rationale: SABATH-family carboxyl methyltransferases are single-domain SAM-dependent methyltransferases with one catalytic activity; GAMT's only known function is GA methyl-esterification.
direction_note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer is effectively irreversible and the enzyme's physiological role is gibberellin inactivation by methyl-esterification, i.e. SAM + GA9 -> SAH + GA9 methyl ester, the council's '>'.

enzyme_name: Gibberellin A4 carboxyl methyltransferase GAMT1/GAMT2 (SABATH family, EC 2.1.1.276)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana (AraCyc cross-reference); gibberellin inactivation II (methylation).
rationale: Same SABATH-family single-activity methyltransferase as rxn21726, here acting on GA4. Note the ModelSEED definition mislabels the product as 'GA4' although cpd23358 is MetaCyc CPD-12332, GA4 methyl ester.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methyl esterification is one-way toward the inactive GA4 methyl ester, the council's '>'.

enzyme_name: Gibberellin carboxyl methyltransferase GAMT1/GAMT2 (SABATH family, EC 2.1.1.-)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana (AraCyc cross-reference); GA20 methylation in gibberellin inactivation II.
rationale: MetaCyc gives only a partial EC (2.1.1.-) for the GA20 substrate, but the reaction sits in the same GAMT-catalysed methylation pathway; SABATH carboxyl methyltransferases are single-domain, single-activity enzymes.
direction_note: SAM -> SAH methyl transfer runs only toward the GA20 methyl ester, the council's '>'.

enzyme_name: Gibberellin carboxyl methyltransferase GAMT1/GAMT2 (SABATH family, EC 2.1.1.-)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana (AraCyc cross-reference); GA34 methylation in gibberellin inactivation II.
rationale: Partial EC only (2.1.1.-), but the step belongs to the GAMT methylation pathway; SABATH-family carboxyl methyltransferases carry a single catalytic activity.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methyl esterification is irreversible toward the GA34 methyl ester, the council's '>'.

enzyme_name: unknown ('paspalate isomerase', MetaCyc EC 5.3.3.-; no protein or gene identified)
organism_context: Claviceps purpurea ergot alkaloid pathway (ergotamine biosynthesis, PWY-6495); paspalic acid -> D-lysergic acid.
rationale: MetaCyc posits a 'paspalate isomerase' with a partial EC but names no gene or protein; in reconstituted pathways the delta-8,9 -> delta-9,10 shift is attributed either to the CloA P450 oxidation chemistry or to non-enzymatic isomerisation, so no catalysing polypeptide can be classified.
direction_note: The pathway runs paspalic acid -> D-lysergic acid (conjugation of the delta-9,10 ergoline with the carboxylate is the downhill, terminal direction); ModelSEED's '<' would pull the pathway's end product backwards.
